newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: STIC in Indonesia industrial park venture.
newsitem.headline: STIC in Indonesia industrial park venture.

text.p: Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp Ltd (STIC) said on Monday it has entered into an agreement with Indonesian Dharmala group to develop the first phase of a 300-hectare industrial park in Surabaya, Indonesia at about Singapore $285 million.
STIC said in a statement it would lead a consortium of Singapore companies which would own 60 percent of the project. STIC intends to take the largest share of 36 percent.
An Indonesian consortium formed by the Dharmala group would take up the remaining 40 percent stake.
STIC said the first of 100 hectares will be developed over a five year period and construction would start in early 1997.

STIC said an investment and operation company would be incorporated in Indonesia to own and operate the industrial park while a Singapore incorporated company would provide project management, finance, customer and marketing services to support the investment and operation company.
The park will feature factories for rental and sale, an administration building, shops, commercial area and amenities.
The key industries the park will focus on include electronics, electrical, precision engineering, pharmaceutical, aerospace and supporting industries, STIC said.
